abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) has emerged as a promising approach for sharing inductive bias across multiple tasks to enable more efficient learning in text classification. However, training all tasks simultaneously often yields degraded performance of each task than learning them independently, since different tasks might conflict with each other. Existing MTL methods for alleviating this issue is to leverage heuristics or gradient-based algorithm to achieve an arbitrary Pareto optimal trade-off among different tasks. In this paper, we present a novel gradient trade-off approach to mitigate the task conflict problem, dubbed GetMTL, which can achieve a specific tradeoff among different tasks nearby the main objective of multi-task text classification (MTC), so as to improve the performance of each task simultaneously. The results of extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets back up our theoretical analysis and validate the superiority of our proposed GetMTL.

bibliographic.title: Improving Gradient Trade-offs between Tasks in Multi-task Text Classification
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

content.problem: Simultaneous training of multiple tasks often degrades performance because tasks conflict with each other and existing methods achieve only arbitrary Pareto trade-offs.
content.proposed_solution: The authors propose GetMTL, a gradient trade-off method that optimizes update directions near the average task gradient to improve all tasks simultaneously.
dataset_testbed: Amazon Review dataset with 14 product review domains treated as 14 binary classification tasks (22180 training and 5600 test instances)
Topic classification dataset from 20 Newsgroups with 16 newsgroups divided into four 4-way classification tasks

metrics.name: avg_acc
metrics.condition: GetMTL average accuracy over the four topic classification tasks on the 20 Newsgroups dataset

metrics.name: avg_acc
metrics.condition: GetMTL average accuracy over the 14 sentiment classification tasks on the Amazon Review dataset

content.claim: GetMTL outperforms existing multi-task learning methods on both benchmarks by reaching superior average classification accuracy and improving individual task performance.
author_stated_limitations: The method cannot be applied to scenarios with large task sets because per-iteration optimization and backward-propagation overhead becomes too high.
